description:
A local-first desktop email client for people who want a calmer, more private inbox.

Pebble is a desktop mail client built with Rust, Tauri, and React. It keeps mail data, the search index, attachments, rules, and application settings on your device by default.
The app is designed around a few practical ideas:
- Your mailbox should stay readable, fast, and quiet.
- Email workflows should be local-first instead of cloud-dashboard-first.
- Privacy controls should be explicit, visible, and easy to override per message.
- Search, snooze, rules, and a Kanban board should work together instead of living in separate tools.
Pebble currently supports Gmail, IMAP, and experimental Outlook accounts.

Highlights

Local-first privacy
- Local SQLite database for messages, folders, labels, rules, and settings.
- Local Tantivy full-text index for fast search.
- Attachments are stored on disk under the app data directory.
- OAuth tokens and credentials are encrypted with a per-device key.
- No telemetry.
- Network requests are limited to features you configure: mail sync, translation, and optional WebDAV settings backup.

Mail workflow
- Unified inbox across multiple accounts.
- Gmail, IMAP, and experimental Outlook support.
- Threaded and message-list views.
- Archive, delete, star, mark read, batch actions, and restore flows.
- Snooze messages and bring them back later.
- Full-text search and advanced filters.
- Rules engine for automatic organization.

Productivity tools
- Kanban board with Todo, Waiting, and Done columns.
- Command palette and keyboard-first navigation.
- Built-in translation providers with bilingual reading.
- Dark and light themes.
- English and Chinese UI.
- Optional WebDAV backup for settings, rules, Kanban cards, and Kanban notes.
Added
- Added per-account sync ranges (all mail, 30/90/365 days, or a custom number of days) for IMAP, Gmail and Outlook, selectable before the first sync and editable later. Widening the range backfills earlier mail; narrowing it keeps existing local mail (#99, #100).
- Added a grouped sidebar style with a switch back to the classic layout in Appearance settings; the grouped layout keeps every folder reachable (#97).
- Added collapsible recipient chips for messages with many participants, plus file-type icons and card styling for attachments (#97).
Changed
- Strengthened typography in the message list and message detail, and restyled the thread sender card (#97).
Fixed
- Fixed unreadable default links in dark-mode email bodies on macOS WebKit and other webviews (#76, #98).
- Fixed email body styles (including the dark-mode light canvas and authored inline styles) being blocked in packaged builds, where Tauri's injected style-src nonce disabled 'unsafe-inline'.
- Fixed archiving with IMAP when the server Archive folder was selected after the local fallback Archive had been created: archive now targets the server folder, the empty fallback is removed, and the destination UID is recorded so later flag changes target the moved message.
- Fixed replies not joining their original conversation because parsed In-Reply-To/References IDs lacked the angle brackets used by stored Message-IDs. Previously mis-threaded messages are not regrouped.
- Restored attachment cards and downloads inside expanded conversation messages.
- Fixed closing the window during startup quitting the app instead of hiding to the tray; an explicit "quit on close" preference is still respected (#97).
- Pinned the macOS traffic-light buttons to the top-left titlebar corner (#97).
- Hardened sync recovery for range changes: IMAP UIDVALIDITY resets rebuild the mailbox without discarding cached mail outside the range, Gmail replays pending history before switching ranges, and Outlook avoids redundant per-page cache copies (#100).
Upgrade notes
- POP3 cannot filter by date and always syncs all mail. Sync range cutoffs start at midnight UTC.
- Automated tests, package builds and native macOS checks against a local IMAP server cover this release. Live Gmail/Outlook range syncing, POP3 downloads and native Windows/Linux UI have not been exercised.
